what: Route 1 run 1 REPEAT (n=2, same +120 config): also completed the full 13000 ms window cleanly, and again FAILS criterion 2a (step never reaches steady rotation) -- this time worse (7.28 deg/s apart vs 2.49 in run 1). Criterion 2b (settle flat) PASSES this time (0.26 deg/s apart), unlike run 1's 2.07 deg/s fail. This is the second data point, not the first.
verdict: FAIL. Criterion 2 (2a) fails. tau_actuator_s=2.206s must NOT be quoted as settled -- the step phase's own rate was still increasing in magnitude at the end.

run_1_repeat.label: baseline 3000 / step 5000 / settle 5000, +120, max_travel_m=4.0 -- identical to run 1
run_1_repeat.actual_outcome: window_complete (the reason-field bug fixed in commit af5f547f is not yet deployed to this host -- beta87 still reads the old logic). motion_refresh.aborted_early is False, 0 of 128 samples carry travel_guard_tripped:true, phase_transitions land on schedule (0 / 3001.4 / 8012.7 ms), last sample at 13001.353 ms of 13000 ms, cumulative_travel_m 2.7732 of the 4.00 m budget.

analysis_raw.interpretation: tau_actuator_s = |rotation after commanding angular 0| / steady rate during the step. Compare it against the ~1 s decision period: well below means the dead time is dominated by the OBSERVER and damping cannot fix it; comparable or above means real actuator carryover.
analysis_raw.caveats: n is small by construction at ~1 Hz. Do NOT fit a turn-rate law to this, and do NOT reuse omega as a calibration constant -- the 2026-08-26 guarded-turn measurement showed a 2.6x spread on identical stationary parameters.

run_1_repeat.analysis_caveat: tau_actuator_s=2.206s and omega_step_deg_per_s=-6.3877 do not meet criterion 2a and must not be quoted as a clean measurement.

1_report_stream_ready.evidence: started/continuous_started true, ready true, no readiness_reason.

2_step_reaches_steady_rotation_2a.requirement: >=3 informative intervals AND last two step rates agree within 1.5 deg/s
2_step_reaches_steady_rotation_2a.note: The LAST interval's rate (-11.108) is the largest magnitude of the whole step phase -- rotation was still accelerating when the step phase ended, not decaying noise. Worse than run 1's 2.493 deg/s gap on the same configuration.

3_settle_goes_flat_2b.requirement: >=3 informative intervals AND last two settle rates agree within 1.5 deg/s
3_settle_goes_flat_2b.note: Course held nearly flat (57.635 -> 57.810 -> 57.709 degrees) across the last three settle intervals -- a genuine plateau, unlike run 1's 2.066 deg/s fail on the same 5000 ms settle length.

4_containment_and_stop.evidence: 0 of 128 samples outside the 9.0 m corridor. stop_result.ok=true, ack.movement_ok=true.

5_travel_guard_does_not_trip.evidence: 0 of 128 samples carry travel_guard_tripped:true; motion_refresh.aborted_early=False; full window elapsed; cumulative_travel_m 2.7732 of 4.00 m never approached the cap.
5_travel_guard_does_not_trip.caveat: The service's own 'reason' field said 'travel_guard_tripped' at run time -- known-wrong, see docs/evidence-route1-run1-fail-20260830.md. The fix (commit af5f547f) is committed but not yet deployed to this host.

6_gate_disarmed_after_verified.evidence: enabled:false, real_motion_allowed:false, no active session, verified from both the live API and RAW core.config_entries after the documented ~15s propagation delay.

what_the_pair_of_runs_now_suggests.settle_phase: 5000 ms settle appears ADEQUATE -- run 2 shows a genuine flat plateau (0.26 deg/s), which run 1 (2.07 deg/s) did not. n=2, one clean pass, treat as a hint not a conclusion.
what_the_pair_of_runs_now_suggests.step_phase: 5000 ms step appears INSUFFICIENT in BOTH runs -- both times the step phase's final interval showed the rate INCREASING in magnitude relative to the prior interval (run 1: -5.686 -> -8.179; run 2: -3.828 -> -11.108), consistent with the rotation still accelerating through onset lag rather than decaying chord noise around a settled value. This reframes run 1's failure: it is not obviously 'chord noise on ~0.26 m chords' as first hypothesized -- it may be the step phase simply ending before steady rotation is reached, matching the predeclaration's own onset-lag arithmetic (~2 s onset, needing ~5-6 s to reach steady rotation; this run commands for exactly 5 s).
what_the_pair_of_runs_now_suggests.caution: n=2. Do not fit a rate law, do not conclude 5000 ms step is definitively too short, and do not raise step_ms in response -- that is a separate, deliberately-written decision (docs/phase2-route1-predeclared-20260830.md section 4 caps it at 5000 on purpose, precisely so this question could be asked honestly).

safety.corridor: 9.0 m square, re-scanned and re-verified at the mower's live position (5.9796, -5.3895) after a supervised repositioning drive -- see repositioning_drive below.
safety.battery_pct: 43-48 range across the session, draining, not charging -- operator explicitly authorized proceeding.
safety.operator_confirmation: explicit go/no-go confirmation taken immediately before dispatch (on-site, supervising, area clear, blades off)

repositioning_drive.why: Run 1 ended at (7.0501, -7.7336), where area-boundary clearance was only 3.467 m against the 4.50 m required disk (0.77x) -- too tight for this corridor. The mower had to be moved back toward the verified spot near (5.98, -5.24) before the repeat could be dispatched.
repositioning_drive.method: raw_pymammotion_execute_vector_segment, the accepted closed-loop reach profile (docs/accepted-profile.json), verified key-by-key identical to the accepted profile before real dispatch.
repositioning_drive.outcome: Two calls were needed. The first (163.5 degree turn required) staged into two 60-degree turns then stopped safely on turn_budget_infeasible (a narrow translation-budget margin on the final small stage, 0.156m estimated vs 0.148m allowed) -- zero linear commands sent, no error, mower stationary and valid_for_motion the whole time. The second call, reusing the VIO calibration offset from the first (vio_heading_offset_degrees, skipping a redundant calibration drive), completed the remaining turn and drove to target_reached at 0.149 m from (5.98, -5.24) -- inside the 0.15 m tolerance.
